fields.summary: SIP statistics: UDP SIP messages and RTP packets are counted twice, TCP once
fields.description:
*Build:* 5.10.0-commit.3094
*DUT:* 192.168.201.50 (dut-201-50), ANPB
*When:* 2026-10-13, 06:31-06:35 UTC
*Test:* RPG-6119 test cycle, cases A2, A3, C1, C3 (the same result in every UDP/TCP replay of the run)

h3. Configuration

SIP list {{s_r6}} = {{alice@ims.example.net}}; rule {{r6_filter}}: input 1 → output 4, redirect. SIP ports at defaults (A2/A3) or 5070 UDP / 5080 TCP (C1/C3).

h3. Steps

Replay one call per PCAP on port 1 at 50 pps, and read {{show sip stats}} before and after. Each call has 7 SIP messages (INVITE, 100, 180, 200, ACK, BYE, 200) and 5 RTP packets over UDP.

h3. Results

||PCAP||SIP transport||Packets on the wire||Rule delta||{{Processed SIP messages}}||{{Processed RTP packets}}||
|{{a2.pcap}} (A2), {{c1.pcap}} (C1)|UDP|7 SIP + 5 RTP|+12|*+14*|*+10*|
|{{a3.pcap}} (A3), {{c3.pcap}} (C3)|TCP|4 SIP segments (7 messages) + 5 RTP over UDP|+9|+7|*+10*|

h3. Expected

One count per SIP message and per RTP packet, whatever the transport: +7 / +5 for both calls.

h3. Actual

* UDP SIP messages count twice (14 for 7); TCP SIP messages count once (7 for 7).
* RTP packets (always UDP here) count twice (10 for 5).
* The rule's packet counters are correct; only the SIP statistics are off.

{{SIP messages per second}} and {{RTP packets per second}} are probably inflated the same way.

h3. Impact

The statistics overstate UDP traffic by 2×, and TCP and UDP numbers can't be compared. This matters more now that RPG-6119 lets customers debug per transport.

h3. Evidence (attached)

* {{f4_pcaps.tar.gz}}: {{a2.pcap}}, {{a3.pcap}}
* {{f4_udp_double_count_transcript.jsonl}}: {{show sip stats}} before/after and the replays for A2, A3, C1, C3
* {{f4_udp_double_count_results.json}}: per-case deltas
